newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: More than 200 said killed in Sri Lanka fighting.
newsitem.headline: More than 200 said killed in Sri Lanka fighting.

text.p: Tamil Tiger rebels struck back at Sri Lankan forces on Thursday in pre-dawn attacks on two bases in the island's east, killing at least 49 soldiers but losing 160 of their own fighters, military officials said.
The rebels overran a small army camp in eastern Batticaloa district and attacked an air force base in Trincomalee district, destroying a transport plane, the officials said.

The attacks came after government forces last month captured a highway linking two army-held towns in the north of the island with little opposition from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), who controlled large areas to the south and southwest.
The LTTE is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese island's north and east.
On Thursday, about 800 rebels overran Vaunathivu camp in Batticaloa, about 200 km (125 miles) from Colombo, killing at least 49 soldiers and wounding 73, military officials said.
But the rebels lost 160 fighters in the raid, according to reports from ground troops, a military spokesman said.
The LTTE blew up a bridge to delay reinforcements, which did not reach the camp until almost 12 hours after the raid began.
Several civilians also were killed in Batticaloa town by indiscriminate rebel mortar fire, a military spokesman said.

A military spokesman earlier said one airman was killed, four were wounded and a Chinese-made Y-12 transport plane was badly damaged in a rebel attack on China Bay air force base in eastern Trincomalee, some 240 km (150 miles) from the capital Colombo. Earlier reports had said four air force personnel died.
There were many LTTE casualties in the attack, which began at about 11:30 p.m. (1730 GMT) and lasted three hours, he said.
"Four terrorist suicide bombers were killed and a large number of them wounded," the spokesman said. "The terrorists withdrew after we launched ground and air attacks."
Rebel communications monitored by the army indicated the LTTE were seeking urgent medical aid for the wounded, he said.
Military officials said a small group of rebels and suicide bombers had infiltrated the camp, which had come under heavy mortar fire which set the transport plane ablaze.
The LTTE's clandestine Voice of Tigers radio station said the rebels destroyed a Y-12 transport plane and damaged a Mi-24 helicopter gunship in the attack on China Bay.
The radio, monitored by Reuters, said 10 soldiers were killed and 70 wounded in the raid on Vaunathivu.
The LTTE's spokesman in London, Anton Rajah, denied that the rebels had suffered heavy casualties.

"We're still awaiting information on these attacks," he told Reuters by telephone. "But LTTE casualties will no way be near that claimed by the Sri Lankan government, which routinely exaggerates LTTE losses and deliberately hides its own."
Last year, the LTTE overran an important army base on the northeast coast, killing or capturing the camp's 1,000 men and dealing the the military its worst blow in the 13-year war.
In January, the rebels attacked a military base at Paranthan, a key road junction south of Jaffna. The army said 223 soldiers died and the rebels said they lost at least 140.
But the military faced little resistence last month when troops backed by artillery, tanks and air cover moved westwards from northern Vavuniya to link up with forces in Mannar.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the civil war, but the LTTE says the number is higher.
